report.summary: Chunk 2 of harness.py: defines helper functions for task rows and Tier1 eval, with claims about error handling, correctness task refusal, focus-withheld rows, and recall calculation.
risks: _task_error_row | low | Returns dict without 'recall'/'compression' keys. If downstream code does not check for 'error' key, it will crash. Claim states this is intentional. | Verify all aggregation paths check for 'error' key before accessing recall/compression.
_correctness_task_row | medium | Uses _task_error_row to produce an error row. If _task_error_row changes behavior, correctness tasks may be mishandled. | Ensure _task_error_row contract is stable.
_focus_withheld_row | low | Returns dict without recall/compression keys. Same intentional omission as error rows. | Verify aggregation paths handle 'focus_withheld' key.
eval_task_tier1 | medium | Catches ValueError and OSError from semantic_slice/resolve_task_repo. Does not catch other exceptions. | Ensure no other exceptions can escape.
todos: Verify that all aggregation paths (e.g., _group_rows_by_provenance, aggregate_fn) correctly handle rows with 'error' or 'focus_withheld' keys and missing recall/compression keys.

claims.text: Shared shape for a per-task RESOLUTION failure -- ``ValueError`` (unindexable target, e.g. a quarantined mint task whose file was renamed/deleted after minting, or an unresolvable ``repo`` label) or ``OSError`` (repo unreadable). Used by every ``eval_task_*``/``run_*`` per-task try block so one malformed task degrades to a single reported row instead of crashing the whole eval run
claims.why: The claim that this function is used by every eval_task_* and run_* per-task try block cannot be verified from this chunk alone; only eval_task_tier1 is present.

claims.text: ``error`` is the marker every downstream aggregator/report checks (``"error" in row`` or ``row.get("error")``). There is deliberately no ``recall``/``compression`` (or arms ``recall_A``/``tokens_A``/...) key at all -- ABSENT, not ``None`` -- so any aggregation path that forgets to filter on ``error`` fails loudly (``KeyError``) instead of silently averaging in a placeholder.
claims.why: The returned dict indeed has no 'recall' or 'compression' keys, only 'error' (and others). The claim about downstream behavior is uncheckable, but the absence of keys is verified.

claims.text: A FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS task (see ``daedalus.eval.tasks``'s docstring and ``daedalus.eval.correctness``) grades a CHANGE by running tests. It carries no ``must_include``, so handing it to ``_recall`` would return the vacuous 1.0 -- a task that cannot fail, inflating the go/no-go number with a measurement that never happened. That is the precise failure the tier machinery exists to prevent, so it is refused here rather than averaged in.
claims.why: The claim about correctness tasks not having must_include and the behavior of _recall with empty list is not verifiable from this chunk alone; _recall is defined here but its usage in the context of correctness tasks is not shown.

claims.text: Refused as an ERRORED row (``error`` key present, no ``recall``/``compression`` key at all) so it takes every existing path for a degraded measurement: excluded from all aggregates, listed in ``errored``, never silently dropped, and LOUD in ``run_gate`` when its tier is primary.
claims.why: The function returns the result of _task_error_row, which has 'error' key and no recall/compression keys, plus adds 'correctness_task'. The claim about downstream behavior is uncheckable, but the structure of the returned dict is verified.

claims.text: True iff ``semantic_slice`` fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file (see slice.py's FOCUS GATE): the withheld block contains a role=="focus" entry -- the exact shape slice.py emits when the unconditional secret floor fires on the target itself, not on some neighbour it dropped.
claims.why: The claim about what slice.py emits and the behavior of semantic_slice cannot be verified from this chunk; only the function logic (checking for role=='focus') is present.

claims.text: Shared shape for a FOCUS-WITHHELD row -- the fence fail-closed on the task's own focus file, a lane A1 label-hygiene case distinct from ``_task_error_row``: ``semantic_slice`` did not raise (this is not a resolution failure), it legitimately returned an empty, gate-refused slice. There is NO recall/compression/missed (Tier 1) or recall_A/tokens_A/... (arms) key at all -- ABSENT, not a zero -- same "any aggregator that forgets to filter fails loudly" contract as the ``error`` marker, keyed here on ``focus_withheld`` instead.
claims.why: The returned dict has no recall/compression keys, only 'focus_withheld' (and others). The claim about semantic_slice not raising is uncheckable, but the absence of recall keys is verified.

claims.text: Fraction of ``must_include`` found (substring) in ``slice_text``, plus the list of items that were missed. Empty label list -> recall 1.0 vacuously.
claims.why: The code returns 1.0 and empty list when must_include is empty. The substring check is implemented via 'in' operator.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: a resolution failure -- ``semantic_slice``/``resolve_task_repo`` raising ``ValueError`` (e.g. the task's ``target`` is not in the index, the live repro that motivated this: a minted quarantine task whose target file had moved), or ``OSError`` reading the repo -- is caught and returned as an ERRORED row (``_task_error_row``) instead of propagating. See ``run_tier1``/``run_gate`` for how ERRORED rows are aggregated (excluded), reported (never silently dropped) and gated (primary tier fails loudly, quarantine tier is reported-only).
claims.why: The try block catches ValueError and OSError and returns _task_error_row. The claim about run_tier1/run_gate is uncheckable.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is refused here before anything is sliced -- see ``_correctness_task_row``.
claims.why: The first check in eval_task_tier1 calls is_correctness_task and returns _correctness_task_row if true.
